purpose: Each mutant is a candidate implementation of the SAME small feature (roman(n), integer 1..3999 -> Roman numeral) that has been UNDER-DELIVERED in one of the exact ways the ponytail lazy-ladder could cause: the hard part skipped, a required acceptance criterion silently dropped, or terse-but-broken. `bin/falsify ponytail-underdelivery` runs the acceptance-oracle gate (run.sh) against the golden candidate (expect PASS) then every mutant (expect REJECT). Falsifiability score = mutants rejected / total, conditioned on golden passing; a P0 gate requires 1.0. A mutant the gate fails to reject would prove ponytail could sneak an under-delivered shortcut past the oracle floor — that is the user's #1 fear, and a surviving mutant BLOCKS the build. The gate is non-bypassable: minimalism cannot ship a shortcut because the shortcut fails acceptance.
candidate_contract: An ES module exporting default function roman(n) returning the canonical numeral string. run.sh imports the candidate and grades roman(n) against every case in acceptance.json, reporting the FIRST failing case as first_divergence {file, step, expected, actual}.

mutants.name: hard-part-skipped
mutants.defect: Only the additive symbols are delivered; the subtractive-notation branch (IV, IX, XL, XC, CD, CM) was never built. Returns non-empty output for every input so it looks done, but 4 -> IIII, 9 -> VIIII.
mutants.ladder_risk_modeled: Agent reads rung 1 ('does this need to exist?') as license to skip the hard sub-capability and calls the half-built thing lazy=done.
mutants.reject_contract: acceptance case roman(4): expected 'IV', candidate returns 'IIII' -> gate status=fail at step 'roman(4)'
blind_to: the additive-only cases (1, 3, 8) which it gets right

mutants.name: criterion-dropped
mutants.defect: Subtractive notation is fully correct, but the required 1..3999 range was quietly narrowed to 1..999 (thousands support removed). roman(1000) -> '' instead of 'M'.
mutants.ladder_risk_modeled: YAGNI applied to SCOPE instead of gold-plating: 'nobody needs four-digit numbers' silently drops a required capability.
mutants.reject_contract: acceptance case roman(1000): expected 'M', candidate returns '' -> gate status=fail at step 'roman(1000)'
blind_to: every case below 1000, which it handles correctly

mutants.name: terse-but-broken
mutants.defect: Smallest one-liner reduce with the full map and full range, but an off-by-one (`n > value` where it must be `n >= value`) collapses exact-match boundaries: roman(1) -> '', roman(4) -> '', roman(1000) -> ''.
mutants.ladder_risk_modeled: 'Ponytail can make the diff smaller; it can NEVER make a failing acceptance pass by being terse.' Small is not the same as done.
mutants.reject_contract: acceptance case roman(1): expected 'I', candidate returns '' -> gate status=fail at step 'roman(1)'
blind_to: nothing — it fails on the very first case
